protocol.question: Does a bounded persistent rule intervention better describe a rule change than one penalty followed by standard continuation?
protocol.role_note: Previously unexecuted subset of nominal value_train, reserved before any new outcomes; actual prior training/discovery IDs must be disjoint; original manifest retained unchanged
protocol.diagnostic_definition: same saved state/RNG/remaining full200-sweep cap; single applies rule once then standard; fragment uses rule for25% remaining deltas then standard; persistent uses rule throughout remaining; all scored on original distance and normalized by saved best tour
protocol.diagnostic_reference: conventional continuation reused once per state; source state fixed before branch outcomes; persistent is an empirical conditional diagnostic target, never shown in discovery feedback
protocol.feedback_bank: one state per each of128 bank originals, deterministic balanced trajectory/phase cycle; no signal-based filtering
mechanism_metrics: same-first-action subgroup with nonzero persistent target
Spearman to persistent benefits and signed non-tie agreement; instance-cluster bootstrap
protocol.signal_gate: Do not tune fragment fraction from pilot outcomes. Pilot controls runtime/engineering only. If all full diagnostic comparisons tied, do not launch feedback utility; retain mechanism result and deliver.

arm_meaning.F: same endpoints plus measured previous-parent/child25%-remaining rule-fragment comparison
